items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 26 at 6:47AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Snowfall will be likely through the day. Given the rain
beforehand and the near/above freezing temperatures, snow will
struggle to accumulate immediately but there will be minor
accumulations by this morning. There may be a brief break later
this morning into the early afternoon, likely allowing snow to
gradually melt. Then snow returns Wednesday evening before
diminishing into snow showers Thursday morning.

Additional snow totals around 1 to 2 inches are expected
early this morning in the area

items.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued August 26 at 6:26AM AKDT until August 26 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Visibility less than 1 mile, at times down to 1/4 mile, in
dense fog.

* WHERE...City and Borough of Wrangell, Petersburg Borough, and
Western Kupreanof Island and Kuiu Island.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM AKDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Low visibility could make travel conditions hazardous.
items.areas: Petersburg Borough; Western Kupreanof and Kuiu Island; City and Borough of Wrangell
items.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 26 at 4:08AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
Areas of fog with patchy dense fog have developed this morning
along the Glenn Highway from just north of Anchorage to Palmer and
along the Parks Highway from Wasilla to Willow. Pockets of dense
fog are most likely from the Knik Bridge along the Glenn Highway
to the Glenn/Parks Highway Interchange. Be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility if traveling in these areas. Have headlights
on and reduce speed in areas with fog.
items.areas: Anchorage; Lower Matanuska Valley; Southern Susitna Valley

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued August 25 at 11:47PM AKDT until August 28 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South to southwest winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50
mph expected, mainly near the coast.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta, Western Capes, and Northern Bristol Bay
Coast.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Thursday to 4 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong front will approach the Southwest
Alaska coastline by noon Thursday, bringing winds that are expected
to gust to 50 mph, mainly for coastal a
items.areas: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island; Interior Kuskokwim Delta; Western Capes; Northern Bristol Bay Coast

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued August 25 at 3:48PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
ESFAFC

Locations:

* Yentna and Skwentna River basins
* Rivers, creeks, and streams with headwaters along the western
Talkeetna Mountains.

Timing:

* First Round - Now through tomorrow Morning
* Second Round - Late Thursday Night through Saturday Evening

Rainfall:

* Widespread rainfall of 0.5 to 1.5 inches of rain is likely (70-80%)
across the Susitna Valley late Monday Night through Wednesday
morning. The highest amounts are very likely (80%-90%) to occur
from Petersville east to Talkeetna
items.areas: Hatcher Pass; Western Susitna Valley; Southern Susitna Valley; Central Susitna Valley; Northern Susitna Valley
